Use a staging tenant with two synthetic accounts and leave access logging enabled. Capture account A's request for its profile, then send the same request under account B's test token after replacing only the object identifier. A bounded check can be represented as:

    for object_id in [1841, 1842, 1843]:
        result = GET(BASE + "/api/profile/" + object_id,
                     Cookie=ACCOUNT_B_TEST_TOKEN)
        record_status_and_redacted_body(result)

If one of those fixtures belongs to A and B receives it, the server has failed to enforce ownership. An attacker would generalize the same operation by collecting more identifiers from links, search results, or exports, retaining successful bodies, and parsing names, invoices, document links, and tokens. A session variant copies a token from one browser into a second request and checks whether it remains accepted after logout or password reset. If it does, the token can be replayed against the victim's endpoints.

An intruder may space requests, vary headers, distribute them across accounts, skip noisy errors, and move a compressed collection through another host. Those are evasion and exfiltration methods. Do not practice them in an assessment. Use only the three fixtures, a tester-issued token, and a source address visible to the owner; do not enumerate real users, copy production records, replay another person's cookie, query internal services, or send data away.

Record the baseline request, changed identifier, redacted response, roles, endpoint, version evidence, and timestamp. Preserve logs and notify the owner after the first cross-account result. Recommend server-side authorization on every lookup, tenant-bound queries, short-lived rotated sessions, revocation after logout and password changes, least privilege, rate limits, and alerts for repeated cross-account access.

The short loop demonstrates how a single authorization error can become systematic collection without touching real data. A legitimate tester stops at the first synthetic mismatch; the broader collection and stealth behavior belong only in the risk explanation.
